s: a male given name from English, feminine equivalent Patricia and Patrizia

pathogen.et: From πάθος (páthos, “suffering, pain”) + -γενής (-genḗs, “producer of”). Equivalent to patho- + -gen.

patent.et: Back-formation from Patent or patentiert in early 19th century student slang.

Pate.et: From Middle High German pate, bate, from Medieval Latin pāter spīrituālis. Compare Middle Low German pāde, Old High German pate (“godmother”), Middle High German pfetter (from Old High German pfetiro (“godfather”)). Related to German Pfetter.

s: patience, solitaire (card game for one player)
In ihrer Freizeit legt sie Patiencen.
Patience.et: Late 18th century. Formally from French patience, but the use for a card game is apparently older in German than in French and English.

s: patient (male or of unspecified sex or female)
Der weibliche Patient, der z. B. vom Arzt bewundert werden will, rivalisiert z. B. gleichzeitig mit der Stationsschwester um die Zuwendung des Arztes.

Patina.et: Borrowed from Italian patina. Doublet of Patene and Patine.

Patriot.et: Borrowed from French patriote, from Late Latin patriōta, from Ancient Greek πατριώτης (patriṓtēs).

Patron.et: From Middle High German patrōn, from Latin patrōnus. Doublet of Patrone.

s: agent noun of patzen: someone who often makes blunders
agent noun of patzen: spot, stain, blot
a female given name, equivalent to English Patricia
in stalemate (said of a situation where one player is not in check but still has no legal move)
problematic, forming a case that can be debatably solved

patzen.et: From batzen (“to be soft or sticky; to do surface-level work”), itself from backen (“to stick together; cake”), a sense that derived from the idea of baking.

s: histrionic; gushing; pompous; grandiose (excessively emotional, dramatic, or solemn)
stalemate; tie (situation where two sides are equally strong, often leading to stagnation)
the nuclear stalemate between the blocs
Die Wahl endete mit einem Patt zwischen der regierenden Koalition und der Opposition.
The election ended in a tie between the incumbent coalition and the opposition.
cartridge, round (live ammunition for a gun)
Er hatte noch drei Patronen im Magazin.
He had three rounds left in the magazine.
cartridge case, casing (parts of a round of ammunition exclusive of the projectile)
Die Kugel haben wir nicht gefunden, aber die Patrone liegt hier.
We haven’t found the bullet, but the casing lies right here.
Patrone.et: Borrowed from French patron. The meaning of 'cartridge' developed from 'patron (saint)' > 'pattern' (as in English) > 'standard amount of gunpowder in a case'. Doublet of Patron.

s: pathognomonic (beyond any doubt diagnostic for a particular disease)

Pater.et: Learned borrowing from Latin pater. Doublet of Vater.

s: patronymic (of, pertaining to, or concerning a patronym)
patronymic (derived from the name of the father)

Patronym.et: Borrowed from Ancient Greek πατρονυμικόν (patronumikón, “patronym”), from πατρονυμικός (patronumikós, “patronymic”), from πατήρ (patḗr, “father”) + ὄνυμα (ónuma) (Doric form of ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”)) + -ικός (-ikós).

Patella.et: Borrowed from Latin patella (“a small pan or dish, a plate; the kneepan, patella”), diminutive of patina (“a broad shallow dish, pan”).

patriarchalisch.et: Blend of patriarchal + patriarchisch, or simply from patriarchal + -isch. The three forms remain widely synonymous, though patriarchisch is more often said of people, while patriarchal(isch) is said of societies, etc.

s: additional side lines on the line
a municipality of Upper Austria, Austria

Patiens.et: From Latin patiens. Doublet of Patient.

s: daub (soft coating of mud, plaster etc.)
mess making; an effort that results in making a mess with substances that are muddy, plastery, doughy, and similar

Patene.et: Middle High German patēne, Old High German phatena, Ecclesiastical Latin patena, Ancient Greek πατάνη (patánē, “kind of flat dish”). Doublet of Patina.

„Da haben wir Probleme. Die Zahlen sind alarmierend“, gestand Neuendorf, der auch kein Patentrezept parat hat, wie etwa mehr Mädchen mit Migrationshintergrund gelockt werden könnten.

Patronenhülse.et: Compound of Patrone (“cartridge, round”) + -n- + Hülse (“hull, casing”).

patronage (group or area of activity associated with a particular patron saint)
Getreidegarben oder Wolken mit Regen und Hagel weisen auf ihr Patronat als Wetterheilige hin.
Sheaves of wheat or clouds with rain and hail indicate her patronage as a weather saint.
